    ordered = sorted(items, key=lambda x: -x['score'])

import json
from pages import list_page

# Helper to create items
items = [
    {"id": "a", "score": 10},
    {"id": "b", "score": 10},
    {"id": "c", "score": 9},
    {"id": "d", "score": 8},
    {"id": "e", "score": 8},
    {"id": "f", "score": 7}
]

page, nxt = list_page(items, None, 3)

    {"id": "a", "score": 10},
    {"id": "b", "score": 10},
    {"id": "c", "score": 9}
], "first page incorrect"

# Decode next_cursor and fetch next page
cursor = nxt

    {"id": "d", "score": 8},
    {"id": "e", "score": 8},
    {"id": "f", "score": 7}
], "second page incorrect"
assert nxt2 is None, "no further page"

# Walk all pages ensures all items returned exactly once
pages = []
cursor = None
while True:
    pg, n = list_page(items, cursor, 2)
    pages.extend(pg)
    if n is None:
        break
    cursor = n
assert sorted(pages, key=lambda x: x["id"]) == sorted(items, key=lambda x: x["id"]) , "all items not returned"

# Test size less than 1
try:
    list_page(items, None, 0)
    assert False, "ValueError for size<1 not raised"
except ValueError:
    pass

# Test malformed cursor
try:
    list_page(items, "not a json", 2)
    assert False, "malformed cursor not raised"
except ValueError:
    pass

# Test cursor beyond data
# cursor pointing to last item
last_cursor = json.dumps([items[-1]["score"], items[-1]["id"]])
pg, n = list_page(items, last_cursor, 1)
assert pg == [] and n is None, "cursor beyond data should give empty page"

print("All tests passed")
